title: The Breeder's Son

where.detail: his father's upper paddock, the gate open onto the hill

time: a spring in his boyhood, twenty years before the Steps
last_beat: His father took the gate by the top bar, swung it open onto the hill and stood aside from it, and Darrow rode the bay out through it.

people.did: Got onto the bay nobody could sit by never being where it expected him, and rode it out through the gate his father opened.

facts.fact: As a boy of eleven he had walked at a horse's head since before he could argue, the way a horse-breeder's son is raised in the Edgemoor hills.
He got onto the bay by going sideways into the place it had just left instead of backward, and up the rail to be higher than its eye.
His father, who said nothing about most things, opened the gate for him without a word.
facts.evidence: as he said nothing about most things

title: His Own

where.detail: the road out of the muster town toward Calden at dusk, at the back of the Ninth's string

time: autumn, the year he was sixteen; the years before the Ninth was his
last_beat: He walked at the mare's head down the road at dusk behind the Ninth's string, past the first stone, and the second, and on toward the fifth in the dark.

people.did: Rode his father's long grey mare down off the hill to a Lowmarch muster, led her through the levy's billhooks untouched, told the Ninth's sergeant he was his own son, and walked at her head down the Holloway behind the Ninth's string.

facts.fact: At sixteen he rode the long grey mare down off the Edgemoor hills to a Lowmarch muster, with his father's brand on her and his father's word that the horse was his.
facts.evidence: "She's yours," his father said. "The brand's mine.

facts.fact: He named the grey filly out of the mare Thistle, for standing in the thistles at the top of the far field to be let alone.
facts.evidence: He had named her Thistle for it the spring before

facts.fact: He led the mare through a line of forty levy boys and their billhooks by watching their shoulders rather than the steel, and came out with every hair of her untouched.
facts.evidence: He watched their shoulders, not the steel.

facts.fact: Asked by the Ninth's sergeant whose son he was, he answered that he was his own.
He went down the road toward Calden at dusk at the back of the Ninth's string, on his feet, with his hand under the mare's jaw.
facts.evidence: He walked at her head with his hand under her jaw

codex.name: Thistle
codex.text: A grey filly out of the long grey mare of Darrow's father's, who stood in the thistles at the top of the far field to be let alone; Darrow named her for it the spring before he was sixteen, and his father let the name go by (Tale 1, Piece 2).

codex.name: The Lowmarch muster
codex.text: On a green at the foot of the Edgemoor hill road, where the Calden road goes through: levy boys with billhooks counted by the bell-house clerk, a string of hill greys for the lances to look over, and the lance's own horses picketed beyond the bell-house. At sixteen Darrow led his mare through the levy's line without a hook touching her, and the Ninth's sergeant let him walk her at the back of the string as far as the fifth milestone (Tale 1, Piece 2).

title: Once

where.detail: the road out of the horse fair at dusk, riding with the Ninth

time: the autumn he was first a knight of the Ninth; the years before the Ninth was his
last_beat: The word stayed in the yard. The only thing that followed him out of the fair was the singing.

people.did: Turned a knight a head taller than anyone at the rail in the horse fair's ring by stepping into the place the man had left, heard the youngest of the Ninth say a word of him once and walked on as though he had not, and rode Thistle out of the fair with the Ninth, his father's gift.

facts.fact: The autumn he was first a knight of the Ninth, in the horse fair's ring, he turned a knight a head taller than anyone at the rail by stepping into the place the man had just left and tapping him behind the knee, until the man stood still and laughed.
facts.evidence: He went sideways and a little forward, into the place the big man had just left

facts.fact: The youngest of the Ninth's knights said the word Quickstep of him once, as a jeer, and he walked on to the rail without turning his head.
facts.evidence: he did not turn his head.

facts.fact: The Ninth's sergeant said a man is called what he does twice, and nobody took the word up.
facts.evidence: Call him what he does twice.

facts.fact: At the horse fair his father sold the Ninth every grey in his string but Thistle, and gave her to Darrow; the Ninth's gate went onto her near quarter at noon.
facts.evidence: sold the Ninth every grey in the string but her, and gave her to him

facts.fact: He rode Thistle out of the fair with the Ninth, and the word stayed in the yard.
facts.evidence: The word stayed in the yard.

codex.name: Thistle
codex.text: Came down the hill in his father's string to the horse fair the autumn Darrow was first a knight of the Ninth, and stood in the horse lines with her head down to be let alone; his father sold the Ninth every grey in the string but her and gave her to Darrow, and the Ninth's gate went onto her near quarter at noon (Tale 1, Piece 3).

codex.name: The ring at the horse fair
codex.text: A roped square of trodden earth behind the horse lines at the autumn fair where the lances buy their greys, with a rail for leaning on and a boy to pick up the wooden swords; every lance at the fair puts a man into it against every other, and the rails bet. The autumn Darrow was first a knight of the Ninth he turned a Calden knight a head taller than anyone there until the man stood still and laughed (Tale 1, Piece 3).

keepsake.name: A name said once
keepsake.text: The word Quickstep, said of him once as a jeer by the youngest of the Ninth in a fair's yard; he walked on as though he had not heard it, and it stayed in the yard when the Ninth rode out.
